data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"No purely local reclamation protocol can satisfy the requirement to never silently displace completed evidence when a crash leaves no terminal record; therefore the only safe protocol is not a local lease/log rivalry but a distributed consensus over external witnesses, and the question of adjudicating single-node protocols is founded on a false premise.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The problem permits probabilistic rather than logical 'never', allowing local checksums","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The workspace is implicitly replicated by the problem's determinism, providing implicit witnesses","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Post-hoc idempotent content addressing can detect silent displacement after the fact, relaxing the 'never' constraint","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'no terminal record' clause applies only to terminal output, not to intermediate durable writes","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A single deterministic workspace without external observation is observationally equivalent to an unobserved Schr\u00f6dinger process. Without a terminal record, local protocols cannot distinguish between 'process crashed before sealing' and 'process sealed but record was lost.' This reduces to the asynchronous consensus impossibility for crash-stop failures in a single-node model. The protocol must durably record: a consensus certificate from at least 2f+1 external witnesses attesting that the seal preceded reclamation. Adjudication between lease and log is moot because both are special cases of the same unsafe local-only assumption.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
